messages.text: I'm a full-time college student at MTSU and broke. Can I get food stamps?

Maybe. Students have some extra rules for food assistance (SNAP), so I need a few details to check.

1. Does anyone else live with you and share food? If so, how old are they?
2. Do you have any income before taxes, like a job, and how often are you paid? If so, how much?
I live alone, no one else in my apartment. And I work about 10 hours a week, around $500 a month before taxes. I get paid monthly.

Thanks, that helps. Two more questions:

1. How old are you?
2. What do you pay each month for rent, and do you pay for heating or cooling (or other utilities) separately from your rent?
I'm 20. Rent is $600 and utilities are included, so I don't pay for heat or anything separate.

**Result for food assistance (SNAP): a caseworker needs to look at this.** You can still apply.

**Why**
- Students aged 18 to 49 who are in college at least half time usually can't get SNAP unless they meet an exemption. USDA says so on its [SNAP Eligibility page](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility). Tennessee's rules are in [SNAP Policy 24.27: Students in Higher Education](https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/human-services/documents/Policy%2024.27%20SNAP%20Students%20in%20Higher%20Educ.pdf).
- One exemption is working 20 hours a week. You work about 10, so that one probably doesn't apply. Other exemptions exist, such as caring for a young child. A caseworker can check whether any fit you.
- Your income and rent look fine. Your $500 a month is under the limits for one person ($1,729 before taxes, $1,330 after deductions), using [USDA's 2026-27 limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola).
- If you did meet an exemption, the screener estimates about **$306 a month**. That is only an estimate, and it isn't what you'd get today without an exemption.

**Notes**
- **Savings:** SNAP generally has a $3,000 limit on cash and bank accounts. I didn't ask about yours.
- **Work rules:** Adults without children may get SNAP for only 3 months in 3 years unless they work or train 20 hours a week. These rules changed in 2025, and a caseworker can explain what applies to you.

**Other programs**
- **TennCare:** This looks unlikely. Tennessee generally doesn't cover adults 19 to 64 who aren't pregnant, disabled, raising a child, or former foster youth. You can still apply at [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or at 855-259-0701.
- **WIC:** This doesn't apply, because it's for pregnant women, new mothers, babies, and children under 5.

**Next steps**
- **Apply for SNAP:** Use the [OneDHS portal](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or call 866-311-4287. Tell them you're a student, and ask about exemptions.
- **Free local help:** Dial 211. MTSU may also have a campus food pantry, which is worth asking about while you wait.

This is only a screening. Only the state agency decides, and anyone can apply.

Do you have work-study, or any other detail about your situation that might matter? I can look up the student exemptions if you'd like.
no work-study, I don't think there's anything else. yeah, can you check the exemptions? I'm not sure what would count for me.

I checked Tennessee's student policy, [SNAP Policy 24.27: Students in Higher Education](https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/human-services/documents/Policy%2024.27%20SNAP%20Students%20in%20Higher%20Educ.pdf) from the Tennessee Department of Human Services. A student has to meet at least one of these:

- **Work 20 hours a week.** The policy says "Be employed an average of twenty (20) hours per week or an average of eighty (80) hours per month," and the job must be paid. Your 10 hours a week doesn't reach that.
- **Be in a work-study program.** The work-study has to be approved when you apply and approved for the school term, and you have to actually be working at the job. You said you don't have this.
- **Get a Families First cash grant.** The policy says "Be receiving Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) cash grant." Tennessee's version is Families First.
- **Care for a child.** This covers a child under 6 in your household, or a single parent in school full time with a child under 12. You live alone, so this doesn't apply.
- **Be in a job or training program.** This includes certain programs such as WIOA, Employment and Training (E&T), the Trade Act, and employer-sponsored on-the-job training. These are less common. Think about whether you're in any program like this through a job or a workforce agency.

**What this means for you:** Based on what you've told me, none of these clearly fits right now. So SNAP looks hard for you at the moment, but I can't say for sure. Only a caseworker can decide. The policy also lists other exemptions that I didn't see in full, so it's still worth applying or calling 866-311-4287 to ask.

**Things that could change this:**
- **Hours:** If you can get to an average of 20 paid hours a week (80 a month), you'd meet the work exemption. Your hours may be limited by school, so only do this if it works for you.
- **Work-study:** If you're offered it, ask MTSU's financial aid office. Work-study can count if it's approved when you apply.
- **Half-time enrollment:** The student rule only applies if you're enrolled at least half time. You said you're full time, so it applies to you.

**Other help while you sort this out:**
- Dial **211** for free local help finding food.
- Ask MTSU if there's a campus food pantry. I don't have details on that from my tools.

This is only a screening. Only the state agency decides, and you can apply either way.
